name: phenotype-conversion
title: IFNg secretion and PDL1n->PDL1p conversion
question:
Do active T cells reliably produce the IFNg field that drives tumor phenotype conversion,
and does the downstream PDL1n->PDL1p conversion itself hold at this scale?

study_card.goal: Separate the robust cytokine driver (IFNg secretion) from the slower, scale-limited conversion it causes.
study_card.mechanism: T cells engaging MHCI+ tumors secrete IFNg into a diffusing field; tumors that internalize enough IFNg switch PDL1n->PDL1p.
study_card.expected_result: A measurable IFNg field forms only with active T cells (every seed); PDL1p conversion is directionally higher with T cells but slow at 10 h.
study_card.main_expert_question: What run length / cell count is needed for the PDL1p conversion fraction to separate from growth noise?

biological_summary:
Tumor phenotype conversion is the paper's central mechanism (Hickey, Agmon et al., Cell
Systems 2024): IFNg secreted by engaged CD8+ T cells diffuses through the tissue and drives
proliferative PDL1n (MHC-I-low) tumor cells into an arrested, inflammatory PDL1p (MHC-I-high)
state that stops dividing (negative for cell-cycle markers, G0). The paper shows this
conversion — not the number of kills — is what controls tumor growth, and that more-active
(25% PD1+) T cells convert tumors earlier (~18 h) and more strongly than exhausted (75% PD1+)
T cells. This study isolates the cytokine driver: across 6 seeds active T cells built a
measurable IFNg field in every run while the no-T control stayed at zero — a robust
reproduction of the secretion step. The downstream PDL1p fraction is directionally higher
with T cells; at the tractable ~10 h scale it does not fully separate from growth noise (it
does at larger scale — see efficacy-at-scale), so it is reported honestly here.

expected_behavior.name: active_tcells_secrete_ifng
expected_behavior.en: Active T cells produce a measurable IFNg field in every seed; the no-T control does not.

measure.of: peak IFNg field concentration per seed, with vs without T cells

expect.of: peak IFNg(with T) > 0 for all seeds and == 0 without T

behavior_tests.name: active_tcells_secrete_ifng

measure.of: peak IFNg field (with vs without T cells), 6 seeds

behavior_tests.result: PASS: IFNg field forms in 6/6 seeds with active T cells; 0/6 without

report.title: IFNg secretion and phenotype conversion
report.objective: Show the robust IFNg-secretion driver and characterize the conversion it drives.
report.conclusion:
Active T cells reliably secrete a diffusing IFNg field (6/6 seeds) — the driver of tumor
phenotype transformation. The downstream PDL1p conversion fraction trends higher with T
cells but is not yet separable from growth noise at this scale.
report.caveat:
Conversion fraction is directional only here (higher with T cells in 2/6 seeds); a
paper-scale run is needed for the conversion step itself to reach significance.

readouts: peak IFNg field over time (with vs without T cells), mean ± std
PDL1p tumor fraction over time (secondary; scale-limited)
